title: Ramen So Good, It's to Die For 2
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Masumi Sera, Kogoro Mouri, Sato Miwako, Takagi Wataru) omitted by convention, even though Sato and Takagi go undercover as regular customers ('Satoko'/'Taka-o-kun') to make the arrest -- that's standard procedural action for that recurring pair, consistent with how they're handled in other v3 files. Patrol officers Miyamoto Yumi and Miike Naeko are KEPT as person nodes (not omitted) because their testimony -- tripping over the culprit's thrown hose, the packing tape he also threw away, and Yumi's ex-boyfriend Chukichi's account of a 'click...click' footstep sound -- is itself load-bearing evidence, not incidental background. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object). case_type: murder (unintentional per the culprit's own account, but committed during a robbery, which is the legally operative fact). The old lower-fidelity file (cases/ep827-828...) named the correct culprit (Mizushina) but got the killing method wrong: it says he 'bludgeons Tonda during a struggle,' implying a weapon blow, when the transcript is explicit that she was pushed during the scuffle and died from hitting her head on the edge of the stairs by the entryway -- the rubber garden hose he was seen swinging was never the weapon (no blood was ever found on it) and was actually an improvised vacuum (hose + his own face mask taped over one end, spun overhead for centrifugal suction) used afterward to retrieve the shattered lenses of his own glasses, which broke underfoot during the struggle and which he could not risk leaving at the scene. The old file also omitted Chukichi, Yumi, and Naeko entirely, collapsed the case into 3 events/2 clues, and left out the staged-safe-scratching detail (Mizushina damaged Tonda's safe himself to make the theft look like a random burglary rather than something he only knew to target because he overheard her bragging about the earrings at the ramen shop).

clues.desc: Mizushina used far more soy sauce than his order justified across repeated visits and switched to a different container mid-meal once one ran low -- behavior consistent with searching multiple containers for something hidden inside one of them, not with seasoning food.

The hose had packing-tape residue at one end and no blood despite being suspected as the murder weapon; a breathable mask taped to a hose and swung overhead generates centrifugal suction, explaining how glass shards could be vacuumed off the ground at the scene without a trace.

Frameless lens shards recovered from the ramen shop's water tank matched a pair of glasses purchased about a month before the murder -- tying the shards, and the missing arms and bridge quietly retrieved the next day, to the buyer.

Chukichi described the fleeing figure's footsteps as an uneven 'click...click' rather than a normal double click -- consistent with someone limping while carrying loose debris underfoot, the detail that pointed toward broken glass being collected rather than dropped.
